item.title: Mend for Bitbucket DC: Version 26.5.1.2 (01-June-2026)
item.description:
Unified Agent 26.4.3.1 | Renovate 43.141.3 | Remediate 26.5.1 | Pre-Scan Builder (PSB) 25.8.1

New Features and Updates

  • Added logic to prevent AI scans from running on feature branches during repository integration scans. AI scans will now only run on base branches, ensuring feature branches are excluded from automated AI analysis.

  • (Renovate) Introduced enhanced customization in Renovate Enterprise Cloud, enabling organizations to run custom scripts and configure environment variables and headers. These new capabilities, powered by secure MicroVM technology, provide greater flexibility and control for enterprise users. For more details, refer to the Renovate documentation.

Resolved Issues

  • Fixed an issue where projects specifying .NET 10 in the .csproj file did not resolve dependencies as expected. The system now detects SDK version mismatches, automatically installs the required .NET SDK, and retries dependency resolution to ensure all dependencies are properly detected.

  • Fixed an issue where preserved user agent properties were not enforced during SCM scans, allowing unintended overrides. Now, all relevant properties are correctly handled to ensure consistent enforcement.

item.title: Mend for GitHub Enterprise: Version 26.5.1.2 (01-June-2026)
item.description:
Unified Agent 26.4.3.1 | Renovate 43.141.3 | Remediate 26.5.1 | Pre-Scan Builder (PSB) 25.8.1

New Features and Updates

  • (SAST) Introducing seamless two-way communication between developers and security reviewers on security findings. Developers can now comment on findings directly from their repository, while reviewer comments from the Mend Platform are instantly visible to developers, streamlining collaboration and accelerating issue resolution.

    • For GitHub Enterprise (using the .whitesource file), security actions such as suppressing findings can now be triggered by posting a comment on the PR or issue instead of checking a checkbox. This makes it easier to add context when suppressing a finding and provides clearer feedback confirming that an action was performed.

    • Introduced a new issueType configuration option - findingsIncludingPullRequests - which creates a separate issue for all findings on both base branches and on feature branches with pull requests to base branches.

    • When that option is enabled, developers and security reviewers can communicate directly on security findings without leaving their tools. Developers can add comments on findings from their GitHub Enterprise repository, and comments added by security reviewers in the Mend Platform are automatically synced to the repository. Likewise, comments added in the repository (via a special command) are synced back to the Mend Platform, ensuring conversations stay mirrored and visible in both locations. This eliminates the need for back-and-forth communication through external channels, making it faster and easier to clarify remediation steps and resolve security issues.

    • Introduced the ability for organizations to configure which SAST suppression reasons are available to developers in GitHub by specifying an array in the .whitesource file, enabling enforcement of custom suppression policies.

    • When suppression requests are approved or rejected, the corresponding GitHub issue gets updated.

    • The feature will be rolled out gradually in the next two weeks.

  • Added logic to prevent AI scans from running on feature branches during repository integration scans. AI scans will now only run on base branches, ensuring feature branches are excluded from automated AI analysis.

  • (Renovate) Introduced enhanced customization in Renovate Enterprise Cloud, enabling organizations to run custom scripts and configure environment variables and headers. These new capabilities, powered by secure MicroVM technology, provide greater flexibility and control for enterprise users. For more details, refer to the Renovate documentation.

Resolved Issues

  • Fixed an issue where deleting a GitHub Enterprise organization did not remove the corresponding Mend product/application, resulting in orphaned entries. Now, Mend correctly deletes the product/application when the organization is deleted.

  • (SCA) Fixed an issue where projects specifying .NET 10 in the .csproj file did not resolve dependencies as expected. The system now detects SDK version mismatches, automatically installs the required .NET SDK, and retries dependency resolution to ensure all dependencies are properly detected.

  • (SCA) Fixed an issue where preserved user agent properties were not enforced during SCM scans, allowing unintended overrides. Now, all relevant properties are correctly handled to ensure consistent enforcement.

item.title: Mend for GitHub.com: Version 26.5.2 (14-June-2026)
item.description:
New Features and Updates

  • Introduced a comprehensive Dependency Dashboard in the Renovate Self-hosted Web UI, allowing users to view notes, warnings, detected dependencies, and suggested updates. Users can now take direct actions such as creating or opening pull requests, retrying or rebasing updates, and triggering new Renovate jobs.

Resolved Issues

  • Fixed an issue where repository scans failed when a Git LFS object was missing or inaccessible on the server.

  • Fixed an issue where manual SAST scans could be triggered via the API even if SAST was not enabled for the target repository. The system now correctly verifies repository settings before initiating a scan, ensuring that no check-runs or security reports are generated for repositories without SAST enablement.

item.title: Mend Developer Platform: Version 26.5.2 (14-June-2026)
item.description:
New Features and Updates

  • When adding or removing repos from the Renovate app installation in GitHub, users no longer go through the Developer Platform onboarding flow. Instead, they are redirected to the Developer Platform UI and the repositories are onboarded according to the existing organization settings.

Resolved Issues

  • (Bitbucket) Fixed an issue where Bitbucket installation events for non-reinstalls could incorrectly trigger the de-onboarding of organizations. The system now properly verifies the uninstallation status before removing onboarding data, ensuring that app updates or other standard events do not disrupt the customer's environment.

item.title: Mend Unified Agent: Version 26.5.1 (01-June-2026)
item.description:
Resolved Issues

  • Fixed an issue where the Unified Agent would hang indefinitely when processing compressed offline request files on newer JDK versions, such as Java 21. This was caused by a threading deadlock during decompression. The process has been updated to use a more efficient, non-threaded decompression method, ensuring compatibility across all supported JDK versions and significantly improving processing speed.

item.title: Mend CLI: Version 26.5.1 (01-June-2026)
item.description:
Resolved Issues

  • (SCA) Fixed an issue where only CVSSv3 vulnerability scores were reported in the Mend CLI output regardless of the organization's CVSS settings in the Mend Platform, ensuring accurate and uniform vulnerability profile data based on the configured CVSS version.

item.title: Mend AI: Version 25.12.1 (05-January-2026)
item.description:
New Features and Updates

  • (Premium / Core) Introducing System Prompt Risk (open beta), a new detection and remediation offering by Mend AI, for mitigating risks posed by system prompts used in conversational AI interfaces.

    • A new System Prompt Risk table inventories system prompts and provides quick export/sharing and deep-link side panel for prompt context.

    • System Prompt Risks are integrated into the existing AI Security Risk Factors across Projects and Applications. The classification appears as a Conversational Interface chip, is filterable, and automatically participates in dashboards and workflows.

    • Remediation in the form of a hardened system prompt is available in the System Prompt side panel, providing clear, copy-ready remediation guidance for AppSec engineers and developers.

    • The AI Security Dashboard has been enriched with system prompt risk data.

    • System prompt risk data is also available via API.

item.title: Mend Container: Version 26.5.2 (14-June-2026)
item.description:
Resolved Issues

  • Fixed an issue where workflow violations were incorrectly triggered for suppressed findings during CLI image scans. Suppressed vulnerabilities are now properly excluded from workflow evaluation, ensuring that automated policies and CLI exit codes accurately reflect the project's security status.

  • Fixed an issue where the total number of container findings in the Project Summary did not match the totals shown in the Security > Containers > Findings page, ensuring consistent and accurate reporting across views.

item.title: Mend SAST: Version 26.5.1 (01-June-2026)
item.description:
New Features and Updates

  • (Closed Beta) Mend SAST now supports a new programming language! First as a closed beta program, customers can now analyze Scala projects to even further reduce security risk.

  • Secret scanning now detects hardcoded private keys (*.pem, *.key) and committed certificate files (*.pfx, *.p12). PowerShell scripts (.ps1) are also included in the set of file types scanned by default. Additionally, the engine now detects a broad set of new credential patterns related to Azure Dev Ops products.

  • Added a new "Information Requested" state to suppression requests, enabling reviewers to request additional context from developers and filter these requests from their pending review queue. This update streamlines the review process and improves workflow efficiency.

Resolved Issues

  • Improved accuracy of Dangerous Method detection in Swift.

item.title: Mend SCA: Version 26.5.2 (14-June-2026)
item.description:
New Features and Updates

  • The Dependencies Findings Report — Org-level report generation is now backed by a new scalable reporting pipeline, resolving timeouts and failures experienced by large organizations.

  • The Dependencies Risk report is now available at the organization level in the Mend Platform UI.

item.title: Mend AppSec Platform: Version 26.5.2 (14-June-2026)
item.description:
New Features and Updates

  • (SCA) The Dependencies Findings Report — Org-level report generation is now backed by a new scalable reporting pipeline, resolving timeouts and failures experienced by large organizations.

  • (SCA) The Dependencies Risk report is now available at the organization level in the Mend Platform UI.

Resolved Issues

  • Fixed an issue where active users accessing the Mend Platform via SSO were incorrectly displayed with an "Invited" status instead of "Active" in the Users section. This status now correctly reflects the user's activity.

  • Fixed an issue where Mend CLI scans failed with a timeout error during policy compliance checks. This occurred when backend processing for specific large datasets exceeded the client-side deadline. The fix optimizes server-side policy evaluation to ensure scans complete successfully within the expected timeframe.

  • (Container) Fixed an issue where workflow violations were incorrectly triggered for suppressed findings during CLI image scans. Suppressed vulnerabilities are now properly excluded from workflow evaluation, ensuring that automated policies and CLI exit codes accurately reflect the project's security status.

  • (Container) Fixed an issue where the total number of container findings in the Project Summary did not match the totals shown in the Security > Containers > Findings page, ensuring consistent and accurate reporting across views.
